title: A general theory of quantum measurements
summary: A universal energy eigenvalue equation is proposed in this paper. It is proven that the unique set of eigenfunctions or preferred basis exists for any non-isolated sub-system. Applying the new eigenvalue equation to the relative motion of a hydrogen atom together with the derived relativistic Hamiltonian to quantify the impact of finite proton mass to the fine structure, correction to the fine structure is obtained as a result of the entanglement of the relative motion and the center-of-mass motion, which can be used to verify the correctness of the proposed eigenvalue equation. Applying the equation to the measurement of electron double-slit interference, it is analyzed that the photon packets with Lorentzian spectral lineshape, the domain and state density of the sub-system, and the energy of the incident electron together determines the spontaneous emission rate of the incident electron. Photons generated in this process excite electrons from the valence band to the conduction band of the detector. Corresponding to any emitted or absorbed photon, the sub-system is found to be uniquely determined by maximizing the transition rate. This new principle is valid for atoms too. Closed-form expressions are obtained for the transition rates and example numerical results show good correlation between calculation and the position measurement experiment. The discovered common mechanisms that determine the sub-systems, the preferred bases, and transition rates form the foundation of a new, general, and consistent theory of quantum measurement.

AI.tldr: A universal energy eigenvalue equation is proposed that identifies unique eigenfunctions/preferred bases for non-isolated subsystems, applied to hydrogen atom fine structure corrections and electron double-slit interference measurements, revealing mechanisms for subsystem determination and transition rates.
AI.motivation: To establish a general, consistent theory of quantum measurement by identifying universal principles that determine subsystems, preferred bases, and transition rates in quantum systems, addressing foundational issues in quantum mechanics.
AI.method: Proposes a universal energy eigenvalue equation; proves existence of unique eigenfunctions/preferred bases for non-isolated subsystems; applies to hydrogen atom relative motion with relativistic Hamiltonian to derive fine structure corrections; analyzes electron double-slit interference with photon packets having Lorentzian spectral lineshape; determines subsystems by maximizing transition rates.
AI.result: Derives correction to hydrogen atom fine structure from entanglement of relative and center-of-mass motion; obtains closed-form expressions for transition rates; shows good correlation between calculations and position measurement experiments; establishes that photons generated in interference process excite electrons in detector valence-to-conduction band transitions.
AI.conclusion: The discovered common mechanisms for determining subsystems, preferred bases, and transition rates form the foundation of a new, general, and consistent theory of quantum measurement applicable to both atomic systems and measurement processes.

title: Fundamental questions on robustness and accuracy for classical and quantum learning algorithms
comment: An invited book chapter (submitted June 2025) in \textit{Quantum Robustness in Artificial Intelligence -- Principles and Applications}, part of the Quantum Science and Technology book series, Springer, ed. Muhammad Usman, 2026
summary: This chapter introduces and investigates some fundamental questions on the relationship between accuracy and robustness in both classical and quantum classification algorithms under noisy and adversarial conditions. We introduce and clarify various definitions of robustness and accuracy, including corrupted-instance robustness accuracy and prediction-change robustness, distinguishing them from conventional accuracy and robustness measures. Through theoretical analysis and toy models, we establish conditions under which trade-offs between accuracy and robustness accuracy arise and identify scenarios where such trade-offs can be avoided. The framework developed highlights the nuanced interplay between model bias, noise characteristics, and perturbation types, including relevant and irrelevant perturbations. We explore the implications of some of these results for incompatible noise, adversarial quantum perturbations, the no free lunch theorem, and suggest future methods to examine these problems from the lens of dynamical systems.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes accuracy-robustness trade-offs in classical and quantum classifiers under noise/adversarial conditions, introducing new robustness definitions and establishing conditions for trade-offs.
AI.motivation: To understand fundamental relationships between accuracy and robustness in classification algorithms, particularly under noisy and adversarial conditions, and to clarify different definitions of robustness that go beyond conventional measures.
AI.method: Theoretical analysis and toy models to establish conditions for accuracy-robustness trade-offs, distinguishing between corrupted-instance robustness accuracy and prediction-change robustness, and examining model bias, noise characteristics, and perturbation types.
AI.result: Established conditions under which trade-offs between accuracy and robustness arise, identified scenarios where such trade-offs can be avoided, and developed a framework highlighting the interplay between model bias, noise characteristics, and perturbation types.
AI.conclusion: The analysis reveals nuanced accuracy-robustness relationships with implications for incompatible noise, adversarial quantum perturbations, and the no free lunch theorem, suggesting future investigation through dynamical systems approaches.

title: Geometry of Quantum Logic Gates
summary: In this work, we investigate the geometry of quantum logic gates within the holomorphic representation of quantum mechanics. We begin by embedding the physical qubit subspace into the space of holomorphic functions that are homogeneous of degree one in each Schwinger boson pair $(z_{a_{j}}, z_{b_{j}})$. Within this framework, we derive explicit closed-form differential operator representations for a universal set of quantum gates--including the Pauli operators, Hadamard, CNOT, CZ, and SWAP--and demonstrate that they preserve the physical subspace exactly. Restricting to unit-magnitude variables ($|z| = 1$) reveals a toroidal space $\mathbb{T}^{2N}$, on which quantum gates act as canonical transformations: Pauli operators generate Hamiltonian flows, the Hadamard gate induces a nonlinear automorphism, and entangling gates produce correlated diffeomorphisms that couple distinct toroidal factors. Beyond the torus, the full Segal--Bargmann space carries a natural Kaehler geometry that governs amplitude dynamics. Entanglement is geometrically characterized via the Segre embedding into complex projective space, while topological protection arises from the $U(1)^{N}$ fiber bundle structure associated with the Jordan--Schwinger constraint.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates quantum logic gates through holomorphic representation, deriving differential operator representations for universal gates and analyzing their geometric action on toroidal and Kähler manifolds, with entanglement characterized via Segre embedding.
AI.motivation: To understand quantum logic gates from a geometric perspective using holomorphic representation, revealing how gates act as canonical transformations on toroidal spaces and how entanglement manifests geometrically in complex projective space.
AI.method: Embed qubit subspace into holomorphic functions homogeneous of degree one in Schwinger boson pairs, derive differential operator representations for universal gates, restrict to unit-magnitude variables to reveal toroidal geometry, and analyze geometric structures in Segal-Bargmann space.
AI.result: Explicit closed-form differential operator representations for Pauli operators, Hadamard, CNOT, CZ, and SWAP gates that preserve physical subspace; quantum gates act as canonical transformations on toroidal space with specific geometric actions; entanglement characterized via Segre embedding; topological protection from U(1)^N fiber bundle structure.
AI.conclusion: Quantum logic gates have rich geometric interpretations in holomorphic representation: they act as canonical transformations on toroidal manifolds, entanglement manifests geometrically through Segre embedding, and topological protection arises from fiber bundle structures, providing new geometric insights into quantum computation.

title: Experimental characterization of the hierarchy of quantum correlations in top quark pairs
summary: Recent results from the Large Hadron Collider have demonstrated quantum entanglement of top quark-antiquark pairs using the spin degree of freedom. Based on the doubly differential measurement of the spin density matrix of the top quark and antiquark performed by the CMS collaboration in the helicity and beam bases, we evaluate a set of quantum observables, including discord, steering, Bell correlation, and magic. These observables allow for a quantitative characterization of the quantum correlations present in a top quark--antiquark system, thus enabling an interpretation of collider data in terms of quantum states and their properties. Discord is observed to be greater than zero with a significance of more than 5 standard deviations ($σ$). Evidence for steering is found with a significance of more than 3$σ$. This is the first evidence for steering, and the first observation of discord in a high-energy system. No Bell correlation is observed within the currently probed phase space, in agreement with the theoretical prediction. These results experimentally corroborate the full hierarchy of quantum correlations in top quarks with discord being the most basic form of quantum correlation, followed by entanglement, steering and Bell correlation. The significance of nonzero magic, which is a complementary observable to the quantum-correlation hierarchy, is found to exceed 5$σ$ in several regions of phase space.

AI.tldr: First experimental evidence of quantum steering and observation of discord in top quark-antiquark pairs at LHC, confirming hierarchy of quantum correlations in high-energy physics.
AI.motivation: To quantitatively characterize quantum correlations in top quark-antiquark systems using collider data, enabling interpretation of high-energy physics phenomena in terms of quantum states and their properties.
AI.method: Analysis of CMS collaboration's doubly differential measurement of spin density matrix in helicity and beam bases, evaluating quantum observables including discord, steering, Bell correlation, and magic.
AI.result: Discord observed >0 with >5σ significance; steering evidence found with >3σ significance (first evidence in high-energy system); no Bell correlation observed as predicted; magic significance >5σ in several phase space regions.
AI.conclusion: Experimental corroboration of full hierarchy of quantum correlations in top quarks, with discord as most basic form, followed by entanglement, steering, and Bell correlation, establishing quantum information framework for high-energy physics.

title: Spectral signatures of nonstabilizerness and criticality in infinite matrix product states
summary: While nonstabilizerness (''magic'') is a key resource for universal quantum computation, its behavior in many-body quantum systems, especially near criticality, remains poorly understood. We develop a spectral transfer-matrix framework for the stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE) in infinite matrix product states, showing that its spectrum contains universal subleading information. In particular, we identify an SRE correlation length -- distinct from the standard correlation length -- which diverges at continuous phase transitions and governs the spatial response of the SRE to local perturbations. We derive exact SRE expressions for the bond dimension $χ=2$ MPS ''skeleton'' of the cluster-Ising model, and we numerically probe its universal scaling along the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ critical lines in the phase diagram. These results demonstrate that nonstabilizerness captures signatures of criticality and local perturbations, providing a new lens on the interplay between computational resources and emergent phenomena in quantum many-body systems.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a spectral transfer-matrix framework for analyzing stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE) in infinite matrix product states, revealing universal subleading information and identifying a distinct SRE correlation length that diverges at critical points.
AI.motivation: Nonstabilizerness (magic) is crucial for universal quantum computation but poorly understood in many-body systems near criticality. The authors aim to develop analytical tools to study how this computational resource behaves at quantum phase transitions.
AI.method: Developed a spectral transfer-matrix framework for stabilizer Rényi entropy in infinite matrix product states. Derived exact SRE expressions for bond dimension χ=2 MPS "skeleton" of the cluster-Ising model. Used numerical methods to probe universal scaling along Z₂ critical lines.
AI.result: Identified an SRE correlation length distinct from standard correlation length that diverges at continuous phase transitions. This length governs spatial response of SRE to local perturbations. Demonstrated that nonstabilizerness captures signatures of criticality and local perturbations.
AI.conclusion: Nonstabilizerness provides a new perspective on the interplay between computational resources and emergent phenomena in quantum many-body systems, with SRE correlation length serving as a universal indicator of critical behavior.

title: GKP-inspired high-dimensional superdense coding with energy-time entanglement
summary: Superdense coding, the application of entanglement to boost classical communication capacity, is a cornerstone of quantum communication. In this paper, we propose a high-dimensional superdense coding protocol using energy-time entangled states. These states are biphoton frequency combs, an example of entangled time-frequency Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (TFGKP) states or time-frequency grid states. Inspired by GKP codes, our protocol involves discretizing the continuous time and frequency degrees of freedom and encoding information by time-frequency displacements. This approach leverages the inherently large Hilbert space found in quantum frequency combs, with resilience against both temporal and spectral errors. In addition to describing the theoretical structure of the protocol, we propose an experimental implementation using standard telecommunication components, time-resolving single-photon detectors and a frequency beamsplitter. We also analyze the effect of experimental noise and errors on the channel capacity of the protocol. We demonstrate that for realistic experimental parameters, contemporary technologies satisfy the prerequisites for superdense coding with biphoton frequency combs, achieving a transmission rate of approximately 8.91 bits per transmitted photon (equivalent to 481 distinguishable messages with asymptotically vanishing errors). This more than doubles the previously highest transmission rate of 4 bits achieved by the Kwiat-Weinfurter scheme, while also having competitive optical loss. Furthermore, our results beat the rate achievable using a single-photon frequency comb with identical parameters by 4.6 times. Our protocol thus represents an experimentally feasible application of time-frequency grid states to entanglement-assisted communication, contributing to the active fields of continuous-variable and high-dimensional quantum information.

AI.tldr: High-dimensional superdense coding protocol using energy-time entangled biphoton frequency combs achieves ~8.91 bits/photon, more than doubling previous best rates.
AI.motivation: To leverage the large Hilbert space of quantum frequency combs for boosting classical communication capacity through entanglement-assisted superdense coding, overcoming limitations of previous discrete-variable approaches.
AI.method: Protocol uses energy-time entangled biphoton frequency combs (TFGKP/time-frequency grid states), discretizes continuous time-frequency degrees of freedom, encodes information via time-frequency displacements, and implements with telecom components, time-resolving detectors, and frequency beamsplitters.
AI.result: Achieves transmission rate of ~8.91 bits per transmitted photon (481 distinguishable messages with asymptotically vanishing errors), more than doubling previous 4-bit Kwiat-Weinfurter scheme, with competitive optical loss and 4.6× improvement over single-photon frequency comb with identical parameters.
AI.conclusion: The protocol represents an experimentally feasible application of time-frequency grid states to entanglement-assisted communication, demonstrating practical high-dimensional superdense coding with contemporary technologies and contributing to continuous-variable and high-dimensional quantum information fields.

title: Quantum Theory for General Observers
summary: The principle of relativity is extended to accommodate observers with quantum properties. This results in a new theory that introduces relative quantization rules and novel uncertainty relations, while also elucidating some interpretational problems present in the current formulation of quantum mechanics.

AI.tldr: Extension of relativity principle to quantum observers, introducing relative quantization rules and new uncertainty relations while addressing quantum mechanics interpretational issues.
AI.motivation: To extend the principle of relativity beyond classical observers to include observers with quantum properties, addressing limitations in current quantum mechanics formulation.
AI.method: Extending relativity principle to accommodate quantum observers, developing relative quantization rules and deriving novel uncertainty relations from this framework.
AI.result: Development of a new theoretical framework with relative quantization rules and novel uncertainty relations that clarify interpretational problems in quantum mechanics.
AI.conclusion: Relativity principle can be successfully extended to quantum observers, yielding a more complete framework that resolves interpretational issues in quantum mechanics.

title: Beyond Reinforcement Learning: Fast and Scalable Quantum Circuit Synthesis
summary: Quantum unitary synthesis addresses the problem of translating abstract quantum algorithms into sequences of hardware-executable quantum gates. Solving this task exactly is infeasible in general due to the exponential growth of the underlying combinatorial search space. Existing approaches suffer from misaligned optimization objectives, substantial training costs and limited generalization across different qubit counts. We mitigate these limitations by using supervised learning to approximate the minimum description length of residual unitaries and combining this estimate with stochastic beam search to identify near optimal gate sequences. Our method relies on a lightweight model with zero-shot generalization, substantially reducing training overhead compared to prior baselines. Across multiple benchmarks, we achieve faster wall-clock synthesis times while exceeding state-of-the-art methods in terms of success rate for complex circuits.

AI.tldr: Quantum unitary synthesis method using supervised learning to approximate minimum description length of residual unitaries combined with stochastic beam search for near-optimal gate sequences, achieving faster synthesis times and higher success rates.
AI.motivation: Existing quantum unitary synthesis approaches suffer from misaligned optimization objectives, substantial training costs, and limited generalization across different qubit counts. The exponential growth of combinatorial search space makes exact solutions infeasible.
AI.method: Uses supervised learning to approximate minimum description length of residual unitaries, combines this estimate with stochastic beam search to identify near-optimal gate sequences. Employs lightweight model with zero-shot generalization to reduce training overhead.
AI.result: Achieves faster wall-clock synthesis times while exceeding state-of-the-art methods in success rate for complex circuits across multiple benchmarks. Substantially reduces training overhead compared to prior baselines.
AI.conclusion: The proposed method effectively mitigates limitations of existing approaches by combining supervised learning for description length approximation with stochastic beam search, enabling efficient quantum unitary synthesis with improved generalization and reduced training costs.

title: Phases of matrix-product states with symmetries and measurements: Finite nilpotent groups
summary: We classify phases of one-dimensional matrix-product states (MPS) under symmetric circuits augmented with symmetric measurements and feedforward. Building on the framework introduced in Gunn et al., Phys. Rev. B 111, 115110 (2025), we extend the analysis from abelian and class-2 nilpotent groups to all finite nilpotent groups. For any such symmetry group $G$, we construct explicit protocols composed of $G$-symmetric circuits and measurements with feedforward that transform symmetry-protected topological (SPT) states into the trivial phase and vice versa using a finite number of measurement rounds determined by the nilpotency class of $G$. Although these transformations are approximate, we prove that their success probability converges to unity in the thermodynamic limit, establishing asymptotically deterministic equivalence. Consequently, all SPT phases protected by finite nilpotent groups collapse to a single phase once symmetric measurements and feedforward are allowed. We further show that the same holds for non-normal MPS with long-range correlations, including GHZ-type states. The central technical ingredient is a hierarchical structure of irreducible representations of nilpotent groups, which enables a recursive reduction of non-abelian components to abelian ones. Our results demonstrate that symmetric measurements lead to a complete collapse of both symmetry-protected and non-normal MPS phases for all finite nilpotent symmetry groups.

AI.tldr: All SPT phases protected by finite nilpotent groups collapse to a single phase when symmetric measurements with feedforward are allowed, with transformations becoming asymptotically deterministic in the thermodynamic limit.
AI.motivation: To extend the classification of matrix-product state phases under symmetric circuits with measurements and feedforward from abelian and class-2 nilpotent groups to all finite nilpotent groups, addressing the fundamental question of how symmetric measurements affect topological phases.
AI.method: Construct explicit protocols using G-symmetric circuits and measurements with feedforward that transform SPT states to trivial phase and vice versa. Leverage hierarchical structure of irreducible representations of nilpotent groups to recursively reduce non-abelian components to abelian ones. Use finite number of measurement rounds determined by nilpotency class.
AI.result: All SPT phases protected by finite nilpotent groups collapse to a single phase under symmetric measurements with feedforward. Transformations are approximate but success probability converges to unity in thermodynamic limit, establishing asymptotically deterministic equivalence. Same holds for non-normal MPS with long-range correlations including GHZ-type states.
AI.conclusion: Symmetric measurements lead to complete collapse of both symmetry-protected and non-normal MPS phases for all finite nilpotent symmetry groups, demonstrating fundamental limitations of symmetry protection when measurement and feedforward are permitted.

title: Efficient quantum circuits for high-dimensional representations of SU(n) and Ramanujan quantum expanders
summary: We present efficient quantum circuits that implement high-dimensional unitary irreducible representations (irreps) of $SU(n)$, where $n \ge 2$ is constant. For dimension $N$ and error $ε$, the number of quantum gates in our circuits is polynomial in $\log(N)$ and $\log(1/ε)$. Our construction relies on the Jordan-Schwinger representation, which allows us to realize irreps of $SU(n)$ in the Hilbert space of $n$ quantum harmonic oscillators. Together with a recent efficient quantum Hermite transform, which allows us to map the computational basis states to the eigenstates of the quantum harmonic oscillator, this allows us to implement these irreps efficiently. Our quantum circuits can be used to construct explicit Ramanujan quantum expanders, a longstanding open problem. They can also be used to fast-forward the evolution of certain quantum systems.

AI.tldr: Efficient quantum circuits for high-dimensional SU(n) irreps with gate complexity polynomial in log(N) and log(1/ε), enabling Ramanujan quantum expanders and quantum system fast-forwarding.
AI.motivation: To develop efficient quantum implementations of high-dimensional irreducible representations of SU(n) groups, addressing longstanding problems in quantum information theory including explicit Ramanujan quantum expanders and fast-forwarding quantum evolution.
AI.method: Uses Jordan-Schwinger representation to realize SU(n) irreps in the Hilbert space of n quantum harmonic oscillators, combined with efficient quantum Hermite transform to map computational basis states to oscillator eigenstates.
AI.result: Constructs quantum circuits with gate count polynomial in log(N) and log(1/ε) for implementing high-dimensional SU(n) irreps, where N is dimension and ε is error.
AI.conclusion: Provides efficient quantum implementation of SU(n) irreps enabling solutions to open problems like Ramanujan quantum expanders and quantum system fast-forwarding, with applications in quantum information and simulation.

title: Intractability of Witnessing Entangled Measurements Device Independently
summary: Protocols have been previously proposed to certify the presence of an entangled measurement in a fully device-independent manner. Here, I provide models for these protocols in which the claimed measurement is not entangled, and demonstrate it is always possible to displace entanglement from measurements to measured states for a general class of device-independent scenarios. This indicates that no black-box measurement scenario requires entangled measurements to replicate its behavior, which is relevant to our fundamental understanding of this phenomenon and how to witness it.

AI.tldr: The paper demonstrates that device-independent protocols claiming to certify entangled measurements can be explained by models where entanglement is in the measured states rather than the measurements themselves.
AI.motivation: Previous protocols claimed to certify the presence of entangled measurements in a device-independent manner, but the author questions whether such certification is truly possible or if entanglement can be displaced from measurements to states.
AI.method: The author provides explicit models for existing protocols where the claimed measurement is not entangled, and demonstrates that for a general class of device-independent scenarios, it's always possible to displace entanglement from measurements to the measured states.
AI.result: The paper shows that no black-box measurement scenario requires entangled measurements to replicate its behavior, as entanglement can always be moved from measurements to states in device-independent frameworks.
AI.conclusion: This finding challenges fundamental understanding of how to witness entangled measurements in device-independent scenarios, indicating that current certification methods may not be conclusive.

title: Tomography by Design: An Algebraic Approach to Low-Rank Quantum States
summary: We present an algebraic algorithm for quantum state tomography that leverages measurements of certain observables to estimate structured entries of the underlying density matrix. Under low-rank assumptions, the remaining entries can be obtained solely using standard numerical linear algebra operations. The proposed algebraic matrix completion framework applies to a broad class of generic, low-rank mixed quantum states and, compared with state-of-the-art methods, is computationally efficient while providing deterministic recovery guarantees.

AI.tldr: Algebraic quantum state tomography using structured measurements and matrix completion for efficient, deterministic recovery of low-rank mixed states.
AI.motivation: Quantum state tomography typically requires extensive measurements; this work aims to develop more efficient methods by leveraging structure in quantum states and using algebraic approaches to reduce measurement requirements.
AI.method: Algebraic algorithm that measures specific observables to estimate structured density matrix entries, then uses standard linear algebra operations (matrix completion) to reconstruct remaining entries under low-rank assumptions.
AI.result: The framework applies broadly to generic low-rank mixed states, is computationally efficient compared to state-of-the-art methods, and provides deterministic recovery guarantees.
AI.conclusion: Algebraic matrix completion offers an efficient, deterministic approach to quantum state tomography with reduced measurement requirements for low-rank quantum states.

title: Near-Infrared and Telecommunication-Wavelength Photon-Pair Source in Optical Fiber
summary: We present a photon-pair source in commercially available optical fiber that produces paired photons at telecommunication and near-infrared (NIR) wavelengths. The highly nondegenerate pairs are 700 nm apart: one in the 1500 nm E- and S-band telecommunication range and the other in the 830 nm NIR range. The high non-degeneracy means the photon pairs are far-detuned from Raman noise, resulting in a high coincidence-to-accidental ratio even while operating at room temperature. The source produces two spectrally and spatially distinct phase-matched processes with low spectral cross-talk, distinct transverse spatial modes in the NIR, and a single fundamental spatial mode in the telecommunication range. The source's room-temperature operation, off-the-shelf materials, and multiplexing potential make it promising for deployment in quantum networks.

AI.tldr: Photon-pair source in commercial fiber producing highly nondegenerate pairs (700 nm apart) at telecom (1500 nm) and NIR (830 nm) wavelengths with low Raman noise and room-temperature operation.
AI.motivation: Develop practical photon-pair sources for quantum networks that can operate at room temperature with commercially available materials, avoiding Raman noise issues common in degenerate sources.
AI.method: Utilizes commercially available optical fiber to generate photon pairs via spontaneous parametric processes, creating highly nondegenerate pairs with 700 nm wavelength separation between telecom (1500 nm) and NIR (830 nm) bands.
AI.result: Achieves high coincidence-to-accidental ratio due to far-detuning from Raman noise, produces two spectrally/spatially distinct phase-matched processes with low cross-talk, distinct transverse modes in NIR, and single fundamental mode in telecom range.
AI.conclusion: The room-temperature operation, use of off-the-shelf materials, and multiplexing potential make this photon-pair source promising for practical deployment in quantum networks.

title: Dissipative Quantum Battery in the Ultrastrong Coupling Regime Between Two Oscillators
summary: In this work, we propose an open quantum battery that stores and releases energy by employing a two-mode ultrastrongly coupled bosonic system, with one mode (the charger) coupled to an independent heat reservoir. Our results demonstrate that both the charging energy and ergotropy of the quantum batteries can be significantly enhanced within the ultra-strong coupling regime and across a broader temperature range in transient time. A unidirectional energy flow is achieved by controlling the system's initial state through its two-mode squeezed ground state. Furthermore, we show that the steady-state stored energy, along with its corresponding ergotropy, can be enhanced at larger temperatures and stronger coupling strengths. Notably, a purely beam-splitter or two-mode squeezing interaction yields zero ergotropy. These findings indicate that the enhanced stored energy and ergotropy of the quantum battery arises principally from the combined effects of beam-splitter and parametric amplification (squeezing) couplings. In addition, the presence of the squared electromagnetic vector potential term can prevent a phase transition and achieve a significant charging energy and high ergotropy in the deep-strong coupling regime. The results presented herein enhance our understanding of the operating principles of open bosonic quantum batteries.

AI.tldr: Open quantum battery using two-mode ultrastrongly coupled bosonic system achieves enhanced charging energy and ergotropy in ultra-strong coupling regime through combined beam-splitter and squeezing interactions.
AI.motivation: To develop an open quantum battery system that can store and release energy efficiently by leveraging ultrastrong coupling effects in bosonic systems, addressing the need for enhanced energy storage and extraction capabilities in quantum battery designs.
AI.method: Proposes a two-mode ultrastrongly coupled bosonic system where one mode (charger) couples to an independent heat reservoir. Uses two-mode squeezed ground state for initial state control to achieve unidirectional energy flow. Analyzes combined effects of beam-splitter and parametric amplification (squeezing) couplings.
AI.result: Both charging energy and ergotropy significantly enhanced in ultra-strong coupling regime across broader temperature range in transient time. Steady-state stored energy and ergotropy enhanced at larger temperatures and stronger coupling strengths. Pure beam-splitter or two-mode squeezing interactions yield zero ergotropy. Squared electromagnetic vector potential term prevents phase transition and achieves significant charging energy in deep-strong coupling regime.
AI.conclusion: Enhanced stored energy and ergotropy in quantum batteries arise principally from combined effects of beam-splitter and parametric amplification couplings. The approach enhances understanding of operating principles for open bosonic quantum batteries and demonstrates practical advantages in ultrastrong coupling regimes.

title: Non-Markovian environment induced chaos in optomechanical system
summary: In traditional research, chaos is frequently accompanied by non-linearity, which typically stems from non-linear interactions or external driving forces. However, in this paper, we present the chaotic behavior that is completely attributed to the non-linear back-reaction of non-Markovian environment. To be specific, we derive the dynamical equations of an optomechanical system and demonstrate that the non-linearity (cause of chaos) in the equations arises entirely from the time-domain convolutions (TDCs) induced by non-Markovian corrections. Under Markovian conditions, these TDCs are reduced into constants, thereby losing the nonlinearity and ultimately leading to the disappearance of chaos. Furthermore, we also observe chaos generation in the absence of optomechanical couplings, which further confirms that the non-Markovian effect is the sole inducement of chaos and the environmental parameters play important roles in the generation of chaos. We hope these results may open a new direction to investigate chaotic dynamics purely caused by non-Markovian environments.

AI.tldr: Non-Markovian environments can induce chaos in optomechanical systems through time-domain convolutions, even without optomechanical coupling or traditional nonlinearities.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate that chaos can arise purely from non-Markovian environmental effects rather than traditional nonlinear interactions or external driving forces.
AI.method: Derived dynamical equations for an optomechanical system and analyzed how time-domain convolutions from non-Markovian corrections introduce nonlinearity that causes chaos.
AI.result: Showed that chaos disappears under Markovian conditions (TDCs become constants), and chaos can be generated even without optomechanical coupling, confirming non-Markovian effects as the sole cause.
AI.conclusion: Non-Markovian environments can be the exclusive source of chaotic dynamics, opening new research directions for studying chaos purely induced by environmental memory effects.

title: Non-Markovian environment induced Schrödinger cat state transfer in an optical Newton's cradle
summary: In this manuscript, we study the Schrödinger cat state transfer in a quantum optical version of Newton's cradle in non-Markovian environment. Based on a non-Markovian master equation, we show that the cat state can be transferred purely through the memory effect of the non-Markovian common environment, even without any direct couplings between neighbor cavities. The mechanism of the environment induced cat state transfer is analyzed both analytically and numerically to demonstrate that the transfer is a unique phenomenon in non-Markovian regime. From this example, the non-Markovian environment is shown to be qualitatively different from the Markovian environment reflected by the finite versus zero residue coherence. Besides, we also show the influence of environmental parameters are crucial for the transfer. We hope the cat state transfer studied in this work may shed more light on the fundamental difference between non-Markovian and Markovian environments.

AI.tldr: Schrödinger cat state transfer via non-Markovian environment memory effects in a quantum optical Newton's cradle, without direct cavity couplings.
AI.motivation: To investigate fundamental differences between non-Markovian and Markovian environments by studying quantum state transfer mechanisms, specifically focusing on how memory effects in non-Markovian environments enable Schrödinger cat state transfer without direct couplings.
AI.method: Using a non-Markovian master equation to analyze a quantum optical version of Newton's cradle, with both analytical and numerical approaches to study environment-induced cat state transfer through memory effects.
AI.result: Demonstrated that Schrödinger cat states can be transferred purely through non-Markovian environment memory effects without direct cavity couplings, showing finite residual coherence in non-Markovian regime versus zero coherence in Markovian regime, with environmental parameters playing crucial roles.
AI.conclusion: Non-Markovian environments are qualitatively different from Markovian environments, enabling unique quantum state transfer phenomena through memory effects, with potential implications for understanding fundamental quantum dynamics in open systems.

title: Nonlocality without entanglement in exclusion of quantum states
summary: We study the task of quantum state exclusion, focusing on antidistinguishability and its generalization to $x$-antidistinguishability, under global measurements and local operations with classical communication (LOCC). We also introduce weak and strong notions of antidistinguiahbaility ($x$-antidistinguishability) depending on whether all states or all $x$-tuples are exhaustively eliminated. Our results reveal striking differences between state exclusion and the more familiar task of state discrimination. In particular, we show that LOCC antidistinguishability of multipartite product states is symmetric with respect to the initiating party but this symmetry breaks down for higher-order $x$-antidistinguishability. Most notably, we establish a manifestation of \emph{nonlocality without entanglement} in the context of state exclusion: we prove that three bipartite product states can be globally antidistinguishable while failing to be LOCC antidistinguishable, demonstrating that three is the minimal number of states required for this phenomenon. We further extend this separation to $2$-antidistinguishability and present example exhibiting the same type of nonlocality. At last, we provide an antidistinguishable tripartite product states that are not LOCC antidistinguishable across any bipartition, which ensures the phenomenon of \emph{genuine nonlocality without entanglement} in this framework.

AI.tldr: Quantum state exclusion task studied with antidistinguishability concepts, revealing differences from state discrimination and demonstrating nonlocality without entanglement phenomena.
AI.motivation: To investigate quantum state exclusion tasks, particularly antidistinguishability and its generalizations, and explore differences between state exclusion and state discrimination, especially in the context of LOCC operations and nonlocality phenomena.
AI.method: Introduces x-antidistinguishability concepts (weak and strong variants) under global measurements and LOCC operations. Studies multipartite product states, analyzes symmetry properties, and constructs specific state examples to demonstrate separations between global and LOCC antidistinguishability.
AI.result: LOCC antidistinguishability of multipartite product states is symmetric for initiating party, but symmetry breaks for higher-order x-antidistinguishability. Demonstrates nonlocality without entanglement: three bipartite product states can be globally antidistinguishable but not LOCC antidistinguishable (minimal number). Extends separation to 2-antidistinguishability and presents genuine nonlocality without entanglement across any bipartition for tripartite states.
AI.conclusion: Quantum state exclusion exhibits fundamentally different properties from state discrimination, particularly regarding LOCC operations. The work establishes minimal examples of nonlocality without entanglement in state exclusion framework, revealing genuine multipartite nonlocality phenomena that persist across all bipartitions.

title: Cluster Ising quantum batteries can mimic super-extensive charging power
summary: Quantum batteries, miniaturized devices able to store and release energy on demand, are promising both because their intrinsic energy and time scales can match those of other quantum technologies and due to the intriguing possibility of achieving super-extensive charging power. While this enhanced scaling is known to appear in several settings, it is generally believed to be forbidden in Wigner-Jordan integrable spin chains charged via quantum-quench protocols. Here, we show that an extended cluster-Ising model, despite belonging to the above category, exhibits super-extensive charging power over wide ranges of system sizes, reaching up to a thousand spins, in proper parameter regimes. This remarkable anomalous scaling is due to a corresponding super-extensive growth of the stored energy, implying that it occurs at large but finite size and cannot persist in the thermodynamic limit. This phenomenon appears robust against finite-temperature effects.

AI.tldr: An extended cluster-Ising model exhibits super-extensive charging power in quantum batteries despite being Wigner-Jordan integrable, contrary to previous beliefs.
AI.motivation: Quantum batteries show promise for matching energy/time scales with other quantum technologies and achieving super-extensive charging power. However, this enhanced scaling was believed to be forbidden in Wigner-Jordan integrable spin chains charged via quantum-quench protocols.
AI.method: Study of an extended cluster-Ising model (a Wigner-Jordan integrable spin chain) charged via quantum-quench protocols, analyzing its behavior across wide system sizes up to a thousand spins in proper parameter regimes.
AI.result: The model exhibits super-extensive charging power over wide ranges of system sizes, reaching up to a thousand spins. This anomalous scaling is due to super-extensive growth of stored energy, occurring at large but finite size but cannot persist in the thermodynamic limit. The phenomenon appears robust against finite-temperature effects.
AI.conclusion: Super-extensive charging power can occur in Wigner-Jordan integrable spin chains, contrary to previous beliefs, though this scaling is limited to finite system sizes and does not persist in the thermodynamic limit.

title: Quantum Reservoir Computing for Statistical Classification in a Superconducting Quantum Circuit
summary: We analyze numerically the performance of Quantum Reservoir Computing (QRC) for statistical and financial problems. We use a reservoir composed of two superconducting islands coupled via their charge degrees of freedom. The key non-linear elements that provide the reservoir with rich and complex dynamics are the Josephson junctions that connect each island to the ground. We show that QRC implemented in this circuit can accurately classify complex probability distributions, including those with heavy tails, and identify regimes in correlated time series, such as periods of high volatility generated by standard econometric models. We find QRC to outperform some of the best classical methods when the amount of information is limited. This demonstrates its potential to be a noise-resilient quantum learning approach capable of tackling real-world problems within currently available superconducting platforms. We further discuss how to improve our QRC algorithm in real superconducting hardware to benefit from a much larger Hilbert space.

AI.tldr: Quantum Reservoir Computing using superconducting circuits outperforms classical methods for financial time series analysis with limited data, demonstrating noise-resilient quantum learning on near-term hardware.
AI.motivation: To develop a quantum learning approach capable of tackling real-world statistical and financial problems using currently available superconducting platforms, particularly when classical methods struggle with limited information.
AI.method: Numerical analysis of Quantum Reservoir Computing using a reservoir composed of two superconducting islands coupled via charge degrees of freedom, with Josephson junctions providing non-linear dynamics for complex pattern recognition.
AI.result: QRC accurately classifies complex probability distributions (including heavy-tailed ones), identifies regimes in correlated time series (such as high volatility periods), and outperforms best classical methods when information is limited.
AI.conclusion: QRC demonstrates potential as a noise-resilient quantum learning approach for real-world problems on current superconducting hardware, with opportunities for improvement by leveraging larger Hilbert spaces.

title: Drone delivery packing problem on a neutral-atom quantum computer
summary: Quantum architectures based on neutral atoms have gained significant attention in recent years as specialized computational machines due to their ability to directly encode the independent set constraint on graphs, exploiting the Rydberg blockade mechanism. In this work, we address the Drone Delivery Packing Problem via a hybrid quantum-classical framework leveraging a neutral-atom quantum processing unit (QPU). We reformulate the optimization task as a graph-partitioning problem based on the independent sets (ISs) of a scheduling graph that encodes delivery incompatibilities. Each partition corresponds to deliveries assigned to a single drone, with the objective of minimizing the total number of partitions. While the ISs represent time-feasible schedules, battery-duration constraints are enforced through a classical post-processing routine. This methodology enables the recovery of optimal delivery schedules, provided a sufficient number of samples is collected from the QPU to resolve the solution space. We benchmark the hybrid workflow through numerical emulations and demonstrate its effectiveness on Pasqal's Fresnel QPU, reporting hardware experiments with configurations of up to 100 atoms.

AI.tldr: Hybrid quantum-classical framework using neutral-atom QPU solves Drone Delivery Packing Problem via graph partitioning based on independent sets, with hardware experiments up to 100 atoms.
AI.motivation: Neutral-atom quantum architectures can directly encode independent set constraints via Rydberg blockade, making them suitable for solving combinatorial optimization problems like drone delivery scheduling.
AI.method: Reformulate drone delivery packing as graph partitioning problem using independent sets of scheduling graph; use neutral-atom QPU to find independent sets (time-feasible schedules) with classical post-processing for battery constraints.
AI.result: Demonstrated effectiveness through numerical emulations and hardware experiments on Pasqal's Fresnel QPU with configurations up to 100 atoms; optimal schedules recoverable with sufficient QPU samples.
AI.conclusion: Hybrid quantum-classical approach using neutral-atom QPUs is viable for solving drone delivery packing problems, with practical implementation demonstrated on current quantum hardware.

title: Universal entanglement-inspired correlations
summary: Quantum correlations, crucial for the advantage and advancement of quantum science and technology, arise from the impossibility of expressing a quantum state as a tensor product over a given set of parties. In this work, a generalized notion of correlations via arbitrary products is formulated. Remarkably, as a universal property, the connection between such general products and tensor products is established, allowing one to relate generic non-product states to the common notion of entangled states. We construct the set of free operations for general types of products by extending the local-operation-and-classical-communication paradigm, familiar from standard entanglement theory, thereby establishing a resource theory of correlations for general products. A generalization is provided beyond two factors that can be universally related to multipartite entanglement. Applications that highlight the usefulness of the approach are discussed, such as the factorization of fermionic states, the non-local factorization of multi-photon states into single-photon states, and the interesting possibility of understanding prime numbers as a form of single-party entanglement.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a generalized framework for quantum correlations using arbitrary products beyond tensor products, establishes connections to standard entanglement, creates a resource theory for general correlations, and applies it to fermionic states, multi-photon states, and prime numbers.
AI.motivation: To extend the concept of quantum correlations beyond the traditional tensor product framework, allowing for more general notions of product states and correlations that can capture various physical scenarios beyond standard multipartite entanglement.
AI.method: Formulates generalized correlations via arbitrary products, establishes universal connections between general products and tensor products, constructs free operations by extending LOCC paradigm to general products, and develops a resource theory framework for correlations based on general products.
AI.result: Establishes that generic non-product states can be related to standard entangled states through universal connections between general products and tensor products. Creates a comprehensive resource theory for correlations based on general products with extended LOCC operations.
AI.conclusion: The generalized framework successfully extends entanglement theory to arbitrary products, providing applications in fermionic state factorization, multi-photon state decomposition, and even mathematical connections to prime numbers as single-party entanglement.

title: Observing quantum many-body dynamics in emergent curved spacetime using programmable quantum processors
summary: We digitally simulate quantum many-body dynamics in emergent curved backgrounds using 80 superconducting qubits on IBM Heron processors. By engineering spatially varying couplings in the spin-$\frac12$ XXZ chain, consistent with the low energy description of the model in terms of an inhomogeneous Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, we realize excitations that follow geodesics of an effective metric inherited from the underlying spatial deformation. Following quenches from Néel and few-spin-flip states, we observe curved light-cone propagation, horizon-induced freezing in the local magnetization, and position-dependent oscillation frequencies set by the engineered spatial deformation. Despite strong spatial inhomogeneity, unequal-time correlators reveal ballistic quasiparticle propagation in the spin chain. These results establish large-scale digital quantum processors as a flexible platform for detailed and controlled exploration of many-body dynamics in tunable and synthetic curved spacetimes.

AI.tldr: Digital quantum simulation of quantum many-body dynamics in emergent curved spacetimes using 80 superconducting qubits on IBM Heron processors, demonstrating curved light-cone propagation and horizon effects.
AI.motivation: To establish large-scale digital quantum processors as flexible platforms for exploring many-body dynamics in tunable synthetic curved spacetimes, which are difficult to study with classical simulations.
AI.method: Engineered spatially varying couplings in spin-½ XXZ chains to create inhomogeneous Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid descriptions, using 80 superconducting qubits on IBM Heron processors with digital quantum simulation techniques.
AI.result: Observed curved light-cone propagation, horizon-induced freezing in local magnetization, position-dependent oscillation frequencies, and ballistic quasiparticle propagation despite strong spatial inhomogeneity.
AI.conclusion: Large-scale digital quantum processors provide a flexible platform for detailed and controlled exploration of many-body dynamics in tunable synthetic curved spacetimes, enabling studies of emergent gravitational phenomena in quantum systems.

title: Tight Communication Bounds for Distributed Algorithms in the Quantum Routing Model
summary:
We present new distributed quantum algorithms for fundamental distributed computing problems, namely, leader election, broadcast, Minimum Spanning Tree (MST), and Breadth-First Search (BFS) tree, in arbitrary networks. These algorithms are (essentially) optimal with respect to their communication (message) complexity in the {\em quantum routing model} introduced in [PODC 2025]. The message complexity of our algorithms is $\tilde{O}(n)$ for leader election, broadcast, and MST, and $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{mn})$ for BFS ($n$ and $m$ are the number of nodes and edges of the network, respectively). These message bounds are nearly tight in the quantum routing model since we show almost matching corresponding quantum message lower bounds. Our results significantly improve on the prior work of [PODC 2025], who presented distributed quantum algorithms under the same model that had a message complexity of $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{mn})$ for leader election.
  Our algorithms demonstrate the significant communication advantage that quantum routing has over classical in distributed computing, since $Ω(m)$ is a well-established classical message lower bound for leader election, broadcast, MST, and BFS that applies even to randomized Monte-Carlo algorithms [JACM 2015]. Thus, our quantum algorithms can, in general, give a quadratic advantage in the communication cost for these fundamental problems.
  A main technical tool we use to design our distributed algorithms is quantum walks based on electric networks. We posit a framework for using quantum walks in the distributed setting to design communication-efficient distributed quantum algorithms. Our framework can be used as a black box to significantly reduce communication costs and may be of independent interest. Additionally, our lower-bound technique for establishing distributed quantum message lower bounds can also be applied to other problems.

AI.tldr: New distributed quantum algorithms achieve near-optimal message complexity for fundamental distributed computing problems (leader election, broadcast, MST, BFS) in the quantum routing model, showing quadratic communication advantage over classical algorithms.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate the significant communication advantage of quantum routing over classical distributed computing, where classical algorithms require Ω(m) messages for fundamental problems like leader election, broadcast, MST, and BFS, while quantum algorithms can potentially achieve much lower communication costs.
AI.method: Develop distributed quantum algorithms using quantum walks based on electric networks, creating a framework for using quantum walks in distributed settings as a black box to reduce communication costs. Also establish quantum message lower bounds using new techniques.
AI.result: Achieved message complexity of Õ(n) for leader election, broadcast, and MST, and Õ(√(mn)) for BFS in the quantum routing model. These bounds are nearly tight with matching quantum lower bounds, significantly improving prior work's Õ(√(mn)) for leader election.
AI.conclusion: Quantum routing provides quadratic communication advantage over classical distributed computing for fundamental problems, with quantum walk framework and lower-bound techniques offering tools for designing communication-efficient distributed quantum algorithms.

title: Optimal Classification of Three-Qubit Entanglement with Cascaded Support Vector Machine
summary: We introduce a systematic framework for three-qubit entanglement classification using a cascaded architecture of Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifiers. Leveraging the well defined three-qubit structure with the four nested entanglement classes (S, B, W, and GHZ), we construct three distinct witness models ($\mathcal{M}_{B}$, $\mathcal{M}_{W}$, and $\mathcal{M}_{GHZ}$) that sequentially discriminate between these classes. The proposed Cascaded model achieves an overall classification accuracy of $95\%$ on a comprehensive dataset of mixed states. The framework's robustness and generalization capabilities are confirmed through rigorous testing against out-of-distribution (OOD) entangled states and various quantum noise channels, where the model maintains high performance. A key contribution of this research is an optimization protocol based on systematic feature importance analysis. This approach yields a tunable framework that significantly reduces the number of required features, while maintaining reliable model accuracy.

AI.tldr: A cascaded SVM framework achieves 95% accuracy in classifying three-qubit entanglement into four nested classes (S, B, W, GHZ) through sequential discrimination, with robustness against noise and feature optimization for efficiency.
AI.motivation: To develop a systematic and robust framework for classifying three-qubit entanglement states into well-defined nested classes (S, B, W, GHZ) that can handle mixed states, maintain high accuracy, and generalize well against noise and out-of-distribution states.
AI.method: A cascaded architecture of Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifiers with three distinct witness models (M_B, M_W, M_GHZ) that sequentially discriminate between entanglement classes. Includes systematic feature importance analysis for optimization and feature reduction.
AI.result: Achieves 95% overall classification accuracy on comprehensive mixed state datasets. Demonstrates robustness against out-of-distribution entangled states and various quantum noise channels. Feature optimization enables significant reduction in required features while maintaining reliable accuracy.
AI.conclusion: The cascaded SVM framework provides an effective, robust, and tunable approach for three-qubit entanglement classification with high accuracy and generalization capabilities, featuring an optimization protocol that balances feature efficiency with performance.

title: Theory of temporal three-photon interference
summary: The recent demonstrations of cascaded PDC (CPDC) and the hopeful prospects of realizing third-order PDC (TOPDC) for the generation of three-photon entangled states are paving the way for experimental studies on genuine three-photon interference. In this article, we formulate three-photon interference in terms of ``each three-photon interfering only with itself.'' We show that although a generalized two-alternative three-photon interference setup based on CPDC or TOPDC involves eight different length parameters, the interference can be fully characterized in terms of only three independent parameters. The first parameter is the three-photon path-length difference, which has a direct analog in the one-photon and two-photon cases, and the other two parameters quantify the path-asymmetry length. Unlike two-photon interference, which requires only one parameter to quantify path-asymmetry, two independent parameters are needed in three-photon interference. This results in a broader class of nonclassical three-photon effects, including three-photon HOM-type effects. Our work provides the theoretical basis for existing and future three-photon interference experiments exploring the rich and complex quantum correlations associated with three-particle entanglement and potentially enabling the development of novel protocols for harnessing those correlations.

AI.tldr: Three-photon interference theory shows that genuine three-photon effects require only three independent parameters despite eight possible length configurations, revealing richer quantum correlations than two-photon interference.
AI.motivation: Recent experimental advances in cascaded PDC and third-order PDC enable generation of three-photon entangled states, creating need for theoretical framework to understand genuine three-photon interference phenomena beyond two-photon effects.
AI.method: Formulate three-photon interference using principle of "each three-photon interfering only with itself." Analyze generalized two-alternative three-photon interference setups based on CPDC or TOPDC, reducing eight length parameters to three independent ones: three-photon path-length difference and two path-asymmetry parameters.
AI.result: Three-photon interference requires only three independent parameters (one path-length difference plus two path-asymmetry parameters) compared to two-photon interference's single path-asymmetry parameter. This enables broader class of nonclassical effects including three-photon HOM-type interference patterns.
AI.conclusion: The theoretical framework provides foundation for existing and future three-photon interference experiments, enabling exploration of rich quantum correlations in three-particle entanglement and development of novel protocols harnessing these complex correlations.

title: Magnetically assisted spin-resolved electron diffraction: Coherent control of spin population and spatial filtering
summary: Electron diffraction from nanogratings provides a platform for free-electron interferometry, yet controlled manipulation of electron spin in such geometries remains largely unexplored. In particular, the role of the self-generated magnetic field arising from electron motion and the feasibility of coherent spin control without disrupting diffraction coherence have not been quantitatively investigated. In this article, a self-consistent Maxwell-Pauli framework is developed to study spin-resolved electron diffraction from nanogratings in the presence of magnetic fields. The model incorporates geometric confinement, image-charge interactions, self-generated magnetostatic fields, and externally applied magnetic fields. Numerical simulations show that the intrinsic magnetic self-field produced by the electron probability current is several orders of magnitude too weak to induce measurable spin mixing, demonstrating that nanogratings act as spin-conserving beam splitters under field-free conditions. When a uniform magnetic field is applied upstream of the nanograting, coherent Larmor precession enables controlled spin rotation without modifying the diffraction geometry or degrading coherence. The magnetic field required for a $π$ spin rotation scales inversely with the interaction length and electron de Broglie wavelength $λ_{dB}$. Furthermore, a downstream nonuniform magnetic field applied after the nanograting imparts a spatially varying Zeeman phase, producing opposite transverse momentum shifts for the two spin components. The spin-dependent transverse dynamics is analyzed using Husimi Q-function phase-space maps, which visualize spin-dependent population redistribution and momentum separation. The proposed approach enables tunable spatial separation of spin-resolved free electron beams and establishes an all-magnetic route for coherent spin rotation, control, and interferometry.

AI.tldr: Electron diffraction from nanogratings enables free-electron interferometry with spin control via magnetic fields, showing intrinsic self-fields are negligible while external fields enable coherent spin rotation and spatial separation.
AI.motivation: To investigate controlled manipulation of electron spin in nanograting diffraction geometries, specifically examining the role of self-generated magnetic fields from electron motion and the feasibility of coherent spin control without disrupting diffraction coherence.
AI.method: Developed a self-consistent Maxwell-Pauli framework incorporating geometric confinement, image-charge interactions, self-generated magnetostatic fields, and externally applied magnetic fields. Used numerical simulations to analyze spin-resolved electron diffraction and employed Husimi Q-function phase-space maps to visualize spin-dependent dynamics.
AI.result: Intrinsic magnetic self-field from electron probability current is orders of magnitude too weak for measurable spin mixing, making nanogratings spin-conserving beam splitters. Upstream uniform magnetic fields enable coherent Larmor precession for controlled spin rotation without degrading coherence. Downstream nonuniform magnetic fields produce opposite transverse momentum shifts for spin components, enabling spatial separation.
AI.conclusion: The approach establishes an all-magnetic route for coherent spin rotation, control, and interferometry in free-electron systems using nanogratings, enabling tunable spatial separation of spin-resolved electron beams.

title: Nonlinear Phase Gates Beyond the Lamb-Dicke Regime
summary: Nonlinear phase gates are essential to achieve the universality of continuous-variable quantum processing and its applications. We present a deterministic protocol for generating nonlinear phase gates in trapped ion systems using simultaneous two-tone sideband drives beyond the Lamb-Dicke regime. Our approach harnesses higher-order interaction terms typically neglected or suppressed to construct nonlinear phase gates. This methodology enables high-fidelity gate engineering with a near three-fold reduction in control pulses compared to state-of-the-art theoretical proposals.

AI.tldr: Deterministic protocol for generating nonlinear phase gates in trapped ion systems using simultaneous two-tone sideband drives beyond Lamb-Dicke regime, achieving high fidelity with reduced control pulses.
AI.motivation: Nonlinear phase gates are essential for achieving universality in continuous-variable quantum processing and its applications, but current methods have limitations in efficiency and control complexity.
AI.method: Uses simultaneous two-tone sideband drives beyond the Lamb-Dicke regime, harnessing higher-order interaction terms typically neglected or suppressed to construct nonlinear phase gates.
AI.result: Enables high-fidelity gate engineering with a near three-fold reduction in control pulses compared to state-of-the-art theoretical proposals.
AI.conclusion: The protocol provides an efficient deterministic approach for implementing nonlinear phase gates in trapped ion systems, advancing continuous-variable quantum processing capabilities.

title: Controlling correlations of a polaritonic Luttinger liquid by engineered cross-Kerr nonlinearity
summary: We study correlation properties of polaritons at zero temperature in a multiconnected Jaynes--Cummings (MCJC) lattice on a superconducting circuit quantum electrodynamics platform with engineered cross-Kerr nonlinearity that mimics attractive nearest-neighbour interaction. A multi-connected Jaynes--Cummings lattice is a one-dimensional lattice constructed from alternating qubits and resonators with different left and right couplings. The nearest-neighbour interaction or cross-Kerr coupling is implemented dispersively through ladder-type qutrits between each nearest neighboring pair of resonator modes. Projecting onto the lower-polaritonic manifold, we derive an extended two-mode (bipartite) Bose--Hubbard-like model featuring on-site and attractive nearest-neighbor interactions. Employing a continuum bosonization approach, we express the Hamiltonian in terms of symmetric ($+$) and antisymmetric ($-$) collective modes. In the regime where the ($-$) sector acquires a finite gap, one can reduce the system to an effective single-component Luttinger liquid model for the $+$ sector. The cross-Kerr term reduces the compressibility of the ($+$) mode, thereby enhancing the corresponding Luttinger parameter $K_{+}$, resulting in the slower algebraic decay of single-particle correlations, $G(x)\propto|x|^{-1/(4K_{+})}$.

AI.tldr: The paper studies polariton correlation properties in a multiconnected Jaynes-Cummings lattice on superconducting circuit QED platform with engineered cross-Kerr nonlinearity, deriving an effective Luttinger liquid model showing enhanced algebraic decay of single-particle correlations.
AI.motivation: To investigate correlation properties of polaritons in engineered quantum systems with attractive nearest-neighbor interactions, specifically in multiconnected Jaynes-Cummings lattices implemented on superconducting circuit QED platforms.
AI.method: Construct a one-dimensional multiconnected Jaynes-Cummings lattice with alternating qubits and resonators, implement cross-Kerr coupling via ladder-type qutrits, project onto lower-polaritonic manifold to derive extended two-mode Bose-Hubbard-like model, apply continuum bosonization to express Hamiltonian in symmetric/antisymmetric collective modes, reduce to effective single-component Luttinger liquid model when antisymmetric sector is gapped.
AI.result: Cross-Kerr term reduces compressibility of symmetric mode, enhancing Luttinger parameter K+, leading to slower algebraic decay of single-particle correlations: G(x) ∝ |x|^{-1/(4K+)}.
AI.conclusion: Engineered cross-Kerr nonlinearity in multiconnected Jaynes-Cummings lattices enables control over polariton correlation properties through modification of Luttinger parameters, demonstrating potential for quantum simulation of strongly correlated systems in circuit QED platforms.

title: High-rate Scalable Entanglement Swapping Between Remote Entanglement Sources on Deployed New York City Fibers
summary: Entanglement swapping between photon pairs generated at physically separated nodes over telecommunication fiber infrastructure is an essential step towards the quantum internet, enabling applications such as quantum repeaters, blind quantum computing, distributed quantum computing, and distributed quantum sensing. However, successful networked entanglement swapping relies on generating indistinguishable pairs of photons and preserving them over deployed fibers. This has limited most previous demonstrations to laboratory settings or relied on sophisticated methods to maintain the necessary indistinguishability. Here, we demonstrate a scalable entanglement swapping experiment using naturally indistinguishable entanglement sources based on warm atomic vapor cells. Without sharing lasers or optical frequency references between nodes, nor the need for pulsing the sources, we achieve a swapping rate of nearly 500 pairs/s while maintaining the CHSH parameter above 2. Additionally, we demonstrate the scalability of our method by maintaining the quality of the entanglement swapping on 17.6-km of deployed fibers in NYC, relying on commercially available SPADs at the spoke nodes, SNSPDs at the hub and standard time-synchronization techniques. Our work paves the way for the practical deployment of large-scale hub-and-spoke quantum networks within cities and data centers.

AI.tldr: Demonstration of scalable entanglement swapping using naturally indistinguishable warm atomic vapor cell sources over deployed telecommunication fibers, achieving 500 pairs/s with CHSH > 2 without shared lasers or optical references.
AI.motivation: Entanglement swapping over deployed fiber infrastructure is essential for quantum internet applications (quantum repeaters, distributed quantum computing, etc.), but previous demonstrations have been limited to lab settings or required sophisticated methods to maintain photon indistinguishability.
AI.method: Used naturally indistinguishable entanglement sources based on warm atomic vapor cells, eliminating need for shared lasers or optical frequency references between nodes. Implemented over deployed fibers in NYC using commercially available SPADs at spoke nodes and SNSPDs at the hub with standard time-synchronization techniques.
AI.result: Achieved entanglement swapping rate of nearly 500 pairs/s while maintaining CHSH parameter above 2 (violating Bell inequality). Successfully demonstrated scalability by maintaining entanglement quality over 17.6-km of deployed fibers in NYC.
AI.conclusion: The work demonstrates a practical approach for scalable entanglement swapping using naturally indistinguishable sources, paving the way for deployment of large-scale hub-and-spoke quantum networks within cities and data centers.

title: Generating quantum entanglement from sunlight
summary: Energy consumption is becoming a serious bottleneck for integrating quantum technologies within the existing global information infrastructure. In photonic architectures, considerable energy overheads stem from using lasers, whose high coherence was long considered indispensable for quantum state preparation. Here, we demonstrate that natural, incoherent sunlight can successfully produce quantum-entangled states via spontaneous parametric down-conversion. We detect polarization-entangled photon pairs with a concurrence of $0.905\pm0.053$ and a Bell state fidelity of $0.939\pm0.027$. Importantly, the system violates Bell's inequality with $S=2.5408\pm0.2171$, exceeding the classical threshold of 2, while maintaining generation rates comparable to laser-based setups. These findings pave the way for sustainable quantum applications in resource-limited environments like interplanetary missions.

AI.tldr: Sunlight can generate quantum-entangled photon pairs via spontaneous parametric down-conversion, achieving high entanglement quality comparable to laser-based systems while reducing energy consumption.
AI.motivation: Energy consumption is a major bottleneck for integrating quantum technologies into existing infrastructure. Traditional photonic architectures rely on high-coherence lasers with significant energy overheads, which is unsustainable for resource-limited environments.
AI.method: Using natural, incoherent sunlight as the pump source for spontaneous parametric down-conversion to generate polarization-entangled photon pairs, instead of conventional laser systems.
AI.result: Achieved concurrence of 0.905±0.053, Bell state fidelity of 0.939±0.027, and Bell inequality violation with S=2.5408±0.2171 (exceeding classical threshold of 2), with generation rates comparable to laser-based setups.
AI.conclusion: Incoherent sunlight can successfully produce high-quality quantum-entangled states, enabling sustainable quantum applications in resource-limited environments like interplanetary missions and reducing energy consumption barriers.

title: Meta-Learning for GPU-Accelerated Quantum Many-Body Problems
summary: We explore the industrial and scientific applicability of the VQE-LSTM framework by integrating meta-learning with GPU accelerated quantum simulation using NVIDIA's CUDA-Q (CUDAQ) platform. This work demonstrates how an LSTM-FC meta-initialization module can extend the practical reach of the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) in both chemistry and physics domains. In the chemical regime, the framework predicts ground-state energies of molecular Hamiltonians derived from PySCF, achieving near FCI accuracy while maintaining favorable O(N^2) scaling with molecular size. In the physical counterpart, we applied the same model to quantized Simple Harmonic Motion systems (SHM), successfully reproducing its ground and excited states through VQE and Variational Quantum Deflation (VQD) methods. Benchmark results on NVIDIA GPUs reveal significant speedups over CPU-based implementations, validating CUDAQ's capability to handle large-scale variational workloads efficiently. Overall, this study establishes VQE-LSTM as a viable and scalable approach for GPU accelerated quantum simulation, bridging quantum chemistry and condensed-matter physics through a unified, meta-learned initialization strategy.

AI.tldr: VQE-LSTM framework combines meta-learning with GPU-accelerated quantum simulation using NVIDIA CUDA-Q, achieving near-exact ground-state energies for molecular systems and reproducing quantum harmonic oscillator states with significant speedups over CPU implementations.
AI.motivation: To extend the practical applicability of Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) in both chemistry and physics domains by integrating meta-learning with GPU-accelerated quantum simulation, addressing computational efficiency and scalability challenges.
AI.method: Developed VQE-LSTM framework with LSTM-FC meta-initialization module integrated with NVIDIA CUDA-Q platform. Applied to molecular Hamiltonians from PySCF for chemistry and quantized Simple Harmonic Motion systems for physics, using VQE and Variational Quantum Deflation (VQD) methods.
AI.result: Achieved near Full Configuration Interaction (FCI) accuracy for molecular ground-state energies with favorable O(N²) scaling. Successfully reproduced ground and excited states of quantum harmonic oscillators. GPU benchmarks showed significant speedups over CPU implementations, validating CUDA-Q's efficiency for large-scale variational workloads.
AI.conclusion: VQE-LSTM establishes a viable and scalable approach for GPU-accelerated quantum simulation, bridging quantum chemistry and condensed-matter physics through a unified meta-learned initialization strategy with demonstrated computational efficiency and accuracy.

title: Steady state coherence in a qubit is incompatible with a quantum map
summary: We consider the issue of steady state coherences in a single qubit in the case of a composite system-bath interaction as proposed in \cite{Guarnieri18}. Based on a field theoretical approach we reanalyse the issue within a Redfield description. We find that the Redfield approach in accordance with \cite{Guarnieri18} yields steady state coherences but violating the properties of a quantum map also gives rise to negative populations. The issue is resolved by applying the Lindblad equation which is in accordance with a proper quantum map. The Lindblad equation, however, also implies the absence of steady state coherence.
