We conclude that steady state coherence in a a qubit is incompatible with a quantum map.

AI.tldr: Redfield approach yields steady-state coherences in qubits but violates quantum map properties with negative populations, while Lindblad equation respects quantum maps but eliminates steady-state coherences, showing incompatibility between steady-state coherence and proper quantum maps.
AI.motivation: To reanalyze the issue of steady-state coherences in a single qubit under composite system-bath interactions, examining whether such coherences can exist while maintaining proper quantum map properties.
AI.method: Field theoretical approach with Redfield description analysis, followed by comparison with Lindblad equation to examine quantum map compliance.
AI.result: Redfield approach yields steady-state coherences but produces negative populations violating quantum map properties; Lindblad equation respects quantum maps but eliminates steady-state coherences.
AI.conclusion: Steady-state coherence in a qubit is fundamentally incompatible with a proper quantum map, as quantum map compliance requires Lindblad dynamics which preclude steady-state coherences.

title: Entanglement in the Dicke subspace
summary: In this paper, we provide a complete mathematical theory for the entanglement of mixtures of Dicke states. These quantum states form an important subclass of bosonic states arising in the study of indistinguishable particles. We introduce a tensor-based parametrization where the diagonal entries of these states are encoded as a symmetric tensor, enabling a direct translation between entanglement properties and well-studied convex cones of tensors. Our results bridge multipartite entanglement theory with semialgebraic geometry and the theory of completely positive and copositive tensors. This dictionary maps separability to completely positive tensors, the PPT property to moment tensors, entanglement witnesses to copositive tensors, and decomposable witnesses to sum of squares tensors. Using this framework, we construct explicit PPT entangled states in three or more qutrits. In this class of states, we establish that PPT entanglement exists for all multipartite systems with three qutrits or more, disproving a recent conjecture in [J. Math. Phys. 66, 022203 (2025)]. We also show that, for mixtures of Dicke states, the PPT condition with respect to the most balanced bipartition implies PPT with respect to any other bipartition. We further connect bosonic extendibility of mixtures of Dicke states to the duals of known hierarchies for non-negative polynomials, such as the ones by Reznick and Polya. We thus provide semidefinite programming relaxations for separability and entanglement testing in the Dicke subspace.

AI.tldr: Complete mathematical theory for entanglement of Dicke state mixtures using tensor parametrization, mapping entanglement properties to convex cones of tensors, disproving a PPT entanglement conjecture, and providing SDP relaxations for separability testing.
AI.motivation: To develop a comprehensive mathematical framework for analyzing entanglement in mixtures of Dicke states, which are important bosonic states in indistinguishable particle systems, bridging multipartite entanglement theory with semialgebraic geometry and tensor analysis.
AI.method: Introduces tensor-based parametrization where diagonal entries are encoded as symmetric tensors, creating a dictionary mapping: separability to completely positive tensors, PPT property to moment tensors, entanglement witnesses to copositive tensors, and decomposable witnesses to sum of squares tensors.
AI.result: Constructs explicit PPT entangled states in three or more qutrits, disproves conjecture that PPT entanglement doesn't exist for such systems, shows PPT condition for most balanced bipartition implies PPT for all bipartitions, connects bosonic extendibility to dual hierarchies of non-negative polynomials, and provides SDP relaxations for separability testing.
AI.conclusion: Establishes complete mathematical theory linking Dicke state entanglement to tensor analysis, provides practical tools for entanglement detection via SDP relaxations, and resolves fundamental questions about PPT entanglement existence in multipartite qutrit systems.

title: QwaveMPS: An efficient open-source Python package for simulating non-Markovian waveguide-QED using matrix product states
summary: QwaveMPS is an open-source Python library for simulating one-dimensional quantum many-body waveguide systems using matrix product states (MPS). It provides a user-friendly interface for constructing, evolving, and analyzing quantum states and operators, facilitating studies in quantum physics and quantum information with waveguide QED systems. This approach enables efficient, scalable simulations by focusing computational resources on the most relevant parts of the quantum system. Thus, one can study a wide range of complex dynamical interactions, including time-delayed feedback effects in the non-Markovian regime and deeply non-linear systems, at a highly reduced computational cost compared to full Hilbert space approaches, making it both practical and convenient to model a variety of open waveguide-QED systems (in Markovian and non-Markovian regimes), treating quantized atoms and quantized photons on an equal footing.

AI.tldr: QwaveMPS is an open-source Python library for simulating 1D quantum many-body waveguide systems using matrix product states, enabling efficient study of complex quantum dynamics with reduced computational cost.
AI.motivation: To provide a practical and convenient tool for simulating open waveguide-QED systems that can handle complex dynamical interactions, including time-delayed feedback effects in non-Markovian regimes and deeply non-linear systems, while treating quantized atoms and photons equally.
AI.method: Uses matrix product states (MPS) to efficiently simulate one-dimensional quantum many-body waveguide systems, focusing computational resources on the most relevant parts of the quantum system rather than the full Hilbert space.
AI.result: Developed an open-source Python library with user-friendly interface for constructing, evolving, and analyzing quantum states and operators, enabling highly reduced computational cost compared to full Hilbert space approaches.
AI.conclusion: QwaveMPS provides an efficient, scalable simulation framework for studying a wide range of complex dynamical interactions in waveguide QED systems, making it practical for both Markovian and non-Markovian regimes.

title: Quantum Pontus--Mpemba Effect in Dissipative Quasiperiodic Chains
summary: We investigate how quasiperiodic spatial structure enables protocol-induced acceleration in open quantum systems by analyzing the Pontus-Mpemba effect in one-dimensional chains subject to Markovian dephasing. The dynamics are governed by a Lindblad superoperator that drives all initial states toward a maximally mixed infinite-temperature steady state, isolating dynamical mechanisms from static equilibrium properties. Considering two representative quasiperiodic models, namely a tight-binding chain with a mosaic potential and its extension with power-law long-range hopping, we show that a properly engineered two-step protocol, in which the system is first steered to a finite temperature intermediate state, yields a strictly shorter overall relaxation time than direct evolution from the same initial configuration. This protocol-induced acceleration persists for both initially localized and extended eigenstates and remains robust in the presence of long-range hopping. A Liouvillian spectral analysis reveals that the mechanism originates from a redistribution of spectral weight that suppresses overlap with the slowest decay modes, rather than from any modification of the decay spectrum itself. Our results establish quasiperiodic chains as a controlled setting for engineering relaxation pathways through Liouvillian spectral structure.

AI.tldr: The paper demonstrates how quasiperiodic spatial structure enables protocol-induced acceleration of relaxation in open quantum systems via the Pontus-Mpemba effect, showing that a two-step protocol yields strictly shorter relaxation times than direct evolution.
AI.motivation: To investigate how quasiperiodic spatial structure enables protocol-induced acceleration in open quantum systems, specifically analyzing the Pontus-Mpemba effect in one-dimensional chains subject to Markovian dephasing, isolating dynamical mechanisms from static equilibrium properties.
AI.method: Analysis of two quasiperiodic models: a tight-binding chain with mosaic potential and its extension with power-law long-range hopping. Using a Lindblad superoperator driving all initial states toward a maximally mixed infinite-temperature steady state. Implementing a two-step protocol where the system is first steered to a finite temperature intermediate state, then comparing relaxation times to direct evolution from the same initial configuration.
AI.result: The properly engineered two-step protocol yields strictly shorter overall relaxation time than direct evolution. This protocol-induced acceleration persists for both initially localized and extended eigenstates and remains robust in the presence of long-range hopping. Liouvillian spectral analysis reveals the mechanism originates from redistribution of spectral weight that suppresses overlap with slowest decay modes, not from modification of the decay spectrum itself.
AI.conclusion: Quasiperiodic chains provide a controlled setting for engineering relaxation pathways through Liouvillian spectral structure, demonstrating how protocol-induced acceleration via the Pontus-Mpemba effect can be achieved in quasiperiodic open quantum systems.
